purpose: Deliver a finite open v1.2 product release that provides bounded minimum-quality coverage across the material human-AI collaboration lifecycle, is actually installable and usable on Codex, preserves dynamic native-first capability and carrier adaptation, fills only evidenced residual gaps, survives controlled historical and adversarial counterexamples, and is reproducible and releasable with explicit human authority. The current shortfall corpus is a requirements and counterexample source rather than a feature backlog; coverage permits sufficient native or external reuse and honest degradation, escalation, stop or claim limitation instead of requiring a bespoke Harness mechanism or static perfect score. Natural-task burden reduction, broad real-world effectiveness, distinct-Agent equivalence, and untested operating-system behavior remain continuing field-validation claims rather than release-completion prerequisites. v0.2 remains an immutable bounded calibration milestone, while v1.0 and v1.1 remain immutable stopped zero-outcome attempts; none can satisfy this program by inheritance.

increments.observedProblem: The current terminal expression requires a user-supplied repeated natural-task cohort even though no natural tasks are presently available, leaves the shared human-AI shortfall corpus at reference-only status, and permits no project closeout until external demand appears while the Codex projection remains inactive.
increments.hypothesis: Separating finite product-delivery acceptance from later field-effect validation, while requiring full-chain minimum-quality coverage, evidence-backed native reuse or residual controls, honest unsupported boundaries and a live Codex reference application, will make closeout finite without promoting controlled evidence into real-world value claims or turning the shortfall corpus into a maximalist feature backlog.
increments.falsifier: The revised contract still requires a natural task for completion, equates lifecycle coverage with bespoke implementation or a static perfect score, permits documentation or fixtures alone to prove a control effect, permits acceptance without a working Codex application, or claims real-task burden reduction, cross-Agent equivalence, or broad effectiveness without corresponding field evidence.
increments.stopCondition: The constitution, program, acceptance, verifier, tests, profile/protocol candidates, and public documentation consistently distinguish finite Codex-operational product delivery from non-gating future field validation, with no private cohort activation or stale natural-task completion path.

deliverables: one consistent finite delivery acceptance contract with non-gating field validation
